clock.mode_B_scope: perf_counter wall seconds around solver.solve only, including wrapper work within the call; excludes force-batch updates, recording, statistics, selection and plant integration
clock.alignment: At feedback/solve start, freeze measured state, current goal/reference window and shifted seed. Measure solver.solve wall duration. Replay the OLD active plan for that duration at its existing time since activation; only then activate the selected returned plan at control u0 on arrival. No separate nominal interval is inserted between feedback solves. This sequential offline replay implements the same plant/control behavior as holding the old plan while computation runs; it does not claim GPU/plant computation concurrency or compensate stale initial state.
clock.startup: First task solve starts from the normal initial guess (or explicit TIAGo initial_guess); category startup/cold, selected lane0, activated at simulated t=0. Retain startup wall/native durations; do not charge them to plant. Execute one requested nominal dt prefix, clipped only at terminal overall task boundary; nonterminal goal check occurs after full nominal prefix. Bootstrap active control age is dt at first feedback. This is not the unrelated process/CUDA warm-up required by F01ab; that warm-up is supplied separately.
clock.native_units: solver.solve returns native microseconds; divide by 1000 for milliseconds. Native timing never drives mode B.
clock.substeps: Maximum sim_dt; split at piecewise-constant control-knot boundaries and integrate fractional remainders immediately, with no deferred remainder accumulation.
clock.plan_end: Packed terminal knot is state-only; clamp control selection to knot N-2 and hold the final valid control beyond the horizon.
clock.warm_start: Optimizer trajectory reference origin is previous SOLVE START, not its activation. At next feedback shift the latest selected solved output by feedback_time - previous_optimizer_reference_time, then re-anchor first state to current measured state. The output is a warm seed even if it was discarded from activation at a goal transition. Control sampling separately uses plant_time - active_plan_activation_time; a newly activated plan can have zero control age while its optimizer seed already has nonzero reference age. No stale-state compensation or cost/solver tuning is introduced.
clock.timeout_mode_B: Every nonterminal goal pays the FULL measured solver call duration before another solve or goal switch, even if its requested per-goal deadline lies inside that interval. Check existing reach/timeout gates at actual arrival, record requested deadline, actual goal end and lateness descriptively, then switch goal. Only the final overall reaching-task goal timeout or tracking task/reference end may clip replay; its completed late output is retained but never activated, with full requested arrival and actual shorter execution saved. Old active plan continues aging across nonterminal goal transitions. No new solve before prior call arrival. Bootstrap remains uncharged and no additional solve is performed after its terminal prefix.
clock.timeout_mode_A: Mode A and legacy loops retain checkpoint decisions and timeout conventions, including tracking at-loop-entry duration checks and possible terminal feedback solve. No new A clipping or control-knot splitting is introduced. Reaching retains checkpoint fractional integration correction; legacy tracking retains its original plant-grid sampling, including a step straddling a control knot on noncommensurate grids. Historical cohorts must use their original mode/version.
clock.success_check: Check existing goal/dwell gates at updates; task success and physical compliance remain separate.
clock.interval_gate: No strict deadline gate; share of intervals longer than nominal dt is descriptive only. Preserve terminal clipped interval and identify it in summaries.
clock.reference: Tracking samples its next window at actual feedback/solve-start time, never predicted future arrival. New plans start u0 on arrival as in live plan-arrival policy, despite their stale solve-start state/reference; clocks are recorded separately.
clock.selection: Preserve evaluate_best_trajectory measured-transition provenance: pass prior/current pre-solve feedback states, recorded control and preceding executed interval; do not substitute newly advanced post-computation state. Current V01/T01 B1 selects lane0. No new batch-lane selection or force-estimation policy.

stats.interval_mapping: interval_plan_solve_indices identifies the ACTUALLY EXECUTED active plan: bootstrap solve0 runs nominal startup and first paid compute interval; returned solve1 starts only on arrival. Discarded outputs do not appear as executed plans. All interval arrays retain terminal intervals; feedback-solve arrays retain every performed feedback call, including a completed output that never activates.
stats.raw_solves: record_raw=True: full per-lane state/reference/shifted seed/output, cold/warm/goal_switch category, selected lane, solver telemetry when track_full_stats=True, solve index, feedback_time_s/optimizer_reference_time_s, previous_optimizer_reference_time_s, shift seconds, solve_arrival_time_s, activation_time_s, activation_status, wall seconds/native milliseconds. Requested arrival can lie after clipped task end; discarded outputs retain full duration and bytes.
stats.raw_execution: Every attempted simulated substep has start time, exact step duration, active plan index, active_control_age_s, goal index, full augmented control and state_before. Completed steps retain state_after; failed steps retain errors. Terminal state/time are updated after each successful substep for interrupted evidence. Live applied controls remain unobservable here and need their own histories.
stats.persistence: Campaign uses record_raw=True and persists read-only record_callback events into fresh attempt directories with source/build/input/config hashes. self.last_run_stats is available before startup and includes started/completed/failed records and recording_failure if callback raises. Exceptions propagate; native/plant failures are not successful task outcomes.
